ca_bundle_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA bundle to use for TLS certificate verification. Optional.

client_cert_pem.description: Client certificate to use for authentication. Required when client_key_pem is provided.

client_key_pem.description: Private key associated with the client certificate. Required when client_cert_pem is provided.

endpoint.description: Horizon URL, with protocol (https://) and without trailing slash. Required.

password.description: Local account password. Required when username is provided.

proxy.description: HTTP proxy URL to use for requests. Optional.

skip_tls_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification. Optional, default to false. Note that this is not recommended in production.

username.description: Local account identifier. Required when password is provided.

block.description: The Horizon provider is used to interact with the Horizon API. It can manage the lifecycle of certificates and other resources.

contact_email.description: Contact email associated with the certificate.

csr.description: A CSR (Certificate Signing Request) in PEM format. Providing this attribute will trigger a decentralized enrollment. Incompatible with `subject` and `sans`.

key_type.description: Key type of the certificate. For example: `rsa-2048`.

labels.description: Labels of the certificate, used to enrich the certificate metadata on Horizon.

not_after.description: NotAfter attribute (expiration date) of the certificate.

password.description: Password of the PKCS12 file. Can be provided when using centralized enrollment, or will be generated by Horizon if not set.

password_write_only.description: When true, the PKCS12 password is not persisted to Terraform state. Only meaningful for centralized enrollment. Sensitive material will not be recoverable from state after apply.

pkcs12.description: Base64-encoded PKCS12 file containing the certificate and the private key. Provided when using centralized enrollment.

pkcs12_write_only.description: When true, the PKCS12 value returned/generated for centralized enrollment is not persisted to Terraform state. Only meaningful for centralized enrollment. Sensitive material will not be recoverable from state after apply.

profile.description: Profile where the certificate will be enrolled into.

public_key_thumbprint.description: Public key thumbprint of the certificate.

renew_before.description: How many days before expiration the certificate should be renewed. When a `plan` or `apply` runs inside that window, the provider triggers a renewal on already existing enrollments. For decentralized enrollments, the existing `csr` is reused; if you want a brand-new key on each renewal, regenerate the CSR-producing resource (e.g. `tls_private_key`) so a fresh CSR reaches the renew call.

renewal_trigger.description: Internal marker derived from `not_after`. The provider flips this value to force Terraform to plan a renewal when the `renew_before` window opens. Not meant to be set or referenced by users; it exists only to make renewal plannable.

revocation_date.description: Revocation date of the certificate. Empty when the certificate is not revoked.

revoke_on_delete.description: Whether to revoke certificate when it is removed from the Terraform state or not.

sans.description: Subject alternative names of the certificate. This is ignored when csr is provided.

self_signed.description: Whether this is a self-signed certificate.

signing_algorithm.description: Signing algorithm of the certificate. For example: `SHA256WITHRSA`

element.description: Subject element, followed by a dot and the index of the element. For example: `cn.1` for the first common name.

type.description: Subject element type. For example: `CN` for common name.

value.description: Subject element value. For example: `www.example.com` for common name.

subject.description: Subject elements of the certificate. This is ignored when csr is provided.

wait_for_third_parties.description: Third parties ids to which the certificate will be published.

create.description: A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

block.description: Provides a Certificate resource. This resource allow you to manage the lifecycle of a certificate. To enroll a certificate, you can either provide a CSR (Certificate Signing Request), or a subject and a list of SANs. If you provide a CSR, the enrollment will be decentralized. If you provide a subject and SANs, the enrollment will be centralized.

certificate_pem.description: PEM-encoded X.509 certificate to look up the trust chain for.

chain.description: PEM-encoded certificates returned by Horizon, one entry per certificate, in the requested order.

chain_pem.description: Concatenated PEM bundle of the trust chain, in the requested order.

id.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the concatenated PEM chain returned by Horizon, in the requested order. Two reads with the same input certificate but different `order` values produce different ids.

length.description: Number of certificates in the returned chain.

order.description: Order of the returned chain. One of `leaf_to_root`, `root_to_leaf`, `issuer_leaf_to_root`, `issuer_root_to_leaf`. Defaults to `root_to_leaf`.

block.description: Fetches the trust chain of a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate from Horizon. The chain order returned by Horizon is preserved as-is.
